A lone suited figure, barely three pixels tall at this scale, stands at the basalt cliff edge silhouetted against the banded gas giant filling the entire upper canvas.
A squat observatory dome sits thumbnail-sized at the mesa rim, its slit open and the telescope tube angled toward the nebula dominating the painted sky above.
Two figures in pressure suits stand side by side at middle distance, ant-sized and dwarfed completely by the glacial wall rising two kilometers behind them.
A single lander, legs splayed on the ochre plain, occupies perhaps four millimeters of canvas at the image's lower-left horizon, running lights still visible as faint amber dots.
A collapsed monolith of weathered alien stone lies half-buried in the dune field at mid-canvas, its fallen length suggesting original height far beyond the human scale the painting implies.
A radio-dish array of five receivers sits at the valley floor, each dish the size of a pencil tip, aimed collectively at the pulsar blazing across the upper frame.
A generation-ship hull section curves across the painting's right edge, riveted panels and viewport strips visible yet the whole structure occupying only a narrow band of the cosmic scene.
A suited explorer stands pointing at the glyph-carved cliff face in the mid-ground, their silhouette no taller than a grain of rice against the inscription field stretching forty meters above.
An inflatable habitat module, cream-colored and cylindrical, rests on the permafrost at middle distance, dwarfed to the size of a matchbox by the aurora curtain blazing overhead.
A rover crawls along the distant ridge line at frame edge, its silhouette a tiny beetle-shape leaving a thin track across the rust-colored slope below the canyon rim.
A sand-buried megalith juts from the dune crest at center-distance, its exposed capstone the size of a thumbnail in the painting, hinting at a structure swallowed entirely below.
A small orbital habitat station, its two stub solar panels visible, hangs in the upper-left quadrant of the cosmic vista, barely distinguishable from background stars at this remove.
An abandoned spacecraft husk rests tilted on its side at the plain's far edge, shadow stretching long behind it, occupying perhaps six millimeters of the vast painted landscape.
An orbital-elevator anchor platform sits on the equatorial plain at extreme middle distance, its cable rising vertically until it vanishes into the atmospheric haze above the painted horizon.
A lone observer stands silhouetted in a circular observatory window, visible only as a dark comma-shaped mark against the interior glow, while the quasar erupts across the sky beyond the dome.
A mass-driver track runs diagonally across the painted volcanic plain, its twin rails converging toward a vanishing point at the frame's right edge, launch cradle visible as a tiny cross-shape.
A parked exploration vehicle sits beside a boulder field in the middle ground, roughly the size of a sesame seed at this scale, casting a crisp shadow across the salmon-colored regolith.
A wind-turbine array of six slender towers occupies the ridge at mid-canvas, each turbine a sliver of dark line against the aurora-lit sky, blades feathered and still.
An approaching probe appears at the painting's upper-right corner as a bright delta silhouette the size of a pinhead, its trajectory implying imminent arrival at the ringed world below.
A launch-pad scaffold rises from the crater floor at lower-right, its lattice framework visible as fine dark hatching, dwarfed into insignificance by the comet arc blazing overhead.
A mining outpost of low connected modules huddles at the asteroid's terminator in the painting's mid-ground, its floodlights making a faint smear of yellow against the shadowed regolith.
A suited figure sits on a rock outcropping at middle distance with knees drawn up, silhouetted in profile, occupying a single centimeter of canvas beneath the sweeping Milky Way arch.
A generation-ship observation deck is rendered as a glass-paneled curve in cross-section at the frame's left margin, tiny interior figures visible as dark dashes behind the illuminated panels.
A lone shuttle in transit catches the sun at the painting's zenith, a bright arrowhead no larger than a match-head crossing the vast shadow cast by the planet below.

An abandoned settlement of roofless rectangular foundations covers a hillside at far distance, its grid pattern readable only as faint scored lines against the pale dust, scale implied by their silence.
